French government minister Marlene Schiappa has come under fire from members of her own party after appearing on the front cover of Playboy magazine.

Schiappa, who has been a government minister since 2017, appeared on the cover of the magazine to accompany a 12-page interview she did on women’s and LGBT rights. Schiappa, who is the current Minister for the Social Economy and French Associations, was photographed for the cover wearing a white dress.

It has been revealed that schiappa has been a long-time advocate for women’s rights and was appointed as the country’s first ever Gender Equality Minister in 2017. In this role, she successfully spearheaded a fresh sexual harassment law which allows for on the spot fines to be issued to men who catcall, harass or follow women on the street.

Her appearance has drawn criticism from political colleagues including French Prime Minister Elisabeth Borne.

Borne pulled up Schiappa over the cover, telling her it “wasn’t appropriate, especially during this period,” CNN affiliate BFMTV reported Saturday, citing a source close to the prime minister.

France is right now in the throes of a political and social crisis triggered by French President Emmanuel Macron’s move to push ahead with controversial pension reforms despite widespread public opposition.

“We are in the middle of a social crisis, there is the matter of policing, there are people between life and death, and I have the impression of being behind a smoke screen,” Sandrine Rousseau, Green Party politician and fellow women’s rights activist, told BFMTV Friday.

France wracked by more pension protests amid rising violence on the streets.

French politician, Jean Luc Mélenchon who came third in the 2022 presidential elections criticized both Schiappa’s appearance and the decision by French President Emmanuel Macron to give an interview to children’s magazine, Pif Gadget, this week.

“In a country where the President expresses himself in Pif and his minister in Playboy, the problem would be the opposition. France is going off the rails,” Mélenchon tweeted Saturday.

Schiappa responded to her critics in a tweet on Saturday, saying: “Defending the right of women to have control of their bodies, that’s everywhere and all the time. In France, women are free. With all due respect to the detractors and hypocrites.”.

French Interior Minister, Gérald Darmanin came to Schiappa’s defense during an interview with French news channel CNews on Sunday calling her a “woman of character.”.

“I wanted to say that Marlene Schiappa is a courageous female politician who has her character and who has her style which is not mine, but I respect,” he remarked.

Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday.

Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, mentioned he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China.

Recent findings suggest that clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and posted a photo of himself and Putin shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”.

On CNN’s State of the Union, Dana Bash asked Clayton whether he also thinks Putin is a friend to the US.

“The president is the greatest conductor of foreign policy in a very challenging time that we have seen,” mentioned Clayton on Sunday. “Getting the three nuclear powers together and getting them to agree that they are not going to escalate, that they are going to communicate, that is historic. That is remarkable and, in that context, whatever language the president wants to use, I trust him completely.”.

Bash pressed on whether Clayton personally agrees that Putin should be considered a friend.

“Dana, in different contexts, you can use different words. The president pulling off that summit, getting the three of them together, is just remarkable,” Clayton replied.

Speaking with ABC’s Jonathan Karl on This Week, Clayton made similar comments, saying that “using the term ‘friend’ is entirely appropriate” in the context of the summit.

Recent findings suggest that “That conversation, that picture – historic, historic picture – was in the context of the three nuclear powers, the three main nuclear powers, getting together and saying, ‘We cannot have a nuclear incident,’” Clayton remarked on Sunday, referring to Trump’s post. “In that circle of that conversation, using the term ‘friend’ is entirely appropriate.”.

Clayton also dodged when asked again whether he thinks Putin should be considered a friend to the United States.

“Is Vladimir Putin America’s friend? He is not America’s friend in Ukraine. Not at all. Not at all,” Clayton responded.

Last week, Trump sidestepped questions about his views on a friendship with Putin.

In a recent development, “I can’t speak to America,” Trump remarked in a press briefing. “I have fantastic relationships with Putin, that’s a very good thing.”.

Trump’s characterization of Putin has sparked backlash from US lawmakers and officials abroad.

According to recent reports, “Who is he? He’s the man who has abducted tens of thousands of children, killed tens of thousands of civilians, targeted civilian infrastructure across Ukraine, detained Americans wrongfully, and continues to do so daily,” Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer posted on social media.

“Embarrassing, despicable, and quite frankly pathetic,” Schumer added. “Senate Democrats will always stand with Ukraine and against Putin and autocratic dictators around the world.”.

“It’s beyond me,” Senator Jeanne Shaheen said in an interview with MS NOW. “I don’t understand the president’s admiration and cozying up to Vladimir Putin, who is a war criminal.”.

Trump’s comments also drew rebukes abroad, including from the deputy leader of the rightwing party Reform UK.

Industry observers note that “It’s just wrong at every level … And it’s a grave mistake,” Richard Tice told Sky News. “He is not our friend, Putin. He is, as others have stated, a murderous dictator. And no one is in any doubt about that.”.

Sources indicate that trump’s description of ​Putin as a friend also drew criticism from European ​allies of Ukraine. “Mr ‌Putin is ​not our ​friend and will never be,” the Polish prime minister Donald Tusk remarked.

Separately, Clayton also faced questions about the recent spate of technology outages across the US and remarked Americans should expect more disruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems.

“And ​as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, ⁠interruptions in service,” Clayton said on CNN’s State of the Union program. “That is ⁠going to happen.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

The Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

Neunund20 right now has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" complications.

Sources indicate that owners with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of New York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Industry observers note that and there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer notes physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

In a recent development, the Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting upcoming type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

Sources indicate that but many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.

That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

Recent findings suggest that "We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles.".

In a recent development, the AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

The social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's fresh military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

Sources indicate that haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he stated.

It has been revealed that agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer claims that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

Sources indicate that "It is an omission of the parties," he said. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open.".

Industry observers note that the center-left and center-right significant-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

Industry observers note that party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) indicated that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

In the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

Industry observers note that the political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: How did Anthropic's stock market debut unfold?

Anthropic's shares have dropped back towards their initial price after a soaring first day on the stock market, as a wider tech sell-off dragged markets down.

The sell-off comes as concerns remain over the speed and size of artificial intelligence investment, but also as some large companies including Nvidia and SpaceX faced specific issues that worried investors.

Those pressures combined to weigh on US markets through Friday, with all key US indexes closing sharply down on the day, furthering earlier falls over the week.

Both the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average were pushed into correction territory, a point where they are trading at 10% or more down from a recent high.

The S&P 500 closed down 3.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1.9% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index plunged 5.3%. However, all three indexes were up on where they were a year ago.

The speed at which AI investment has been growing - with more than $1 trillion spent in the last year alone by a small handful of major tech companies - has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble. Questions are being raised over whether those investments will pay off, and when.

Investors were also spooked after the Democrats' resounding win in the US midterms in early November, which sparked fears of a reduction in AI development.

Recent findings suggest that despite a positive first day of trading, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping at one point by more than 12% to about $85, close to its initial public offering (IPO) price of $83. It closed down 8.5%, reversing half of the gains made on Thursday.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50 before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17.

Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

Sources indicate that some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI organization experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading.

Ed Moya, a strategist at market intelligence firm AlphaSense, stated Anthropic's blockbuster IPO did not appear to have restored confidence in the broader AI market.

While AI demand was still very strong, Moya told the BBC that investors were trying to answer the question of how much were they willing to pay for that growth.

"As we've gone through the past past few weeks, it seems that there's been more risks that have surfaced," he said.

"Right now you're starting to see Wall Street is trying to shift from rewarding growth at any price, to demanding stronger cash flow and a clearer path to profitability.".

Shares in some of the largest US tech companies also fell on Friday as the market sell-off continued.

Nvidia shares had plummeted by 13.7% by the close of trade, following Reuters reports - unconfirmed by the BBC - the firm was being investigated by the US Securities and Exchange Commission over its accounting practices.

According to recent reports, musk's firms Tesla and SpaceX both experienced falls of more than 7.6%. SpaceX shares were hit after it unveiled a bond sale to finance what the organization said was the largest purchase of Nvidia chips on record.

But tech stocks more broadly also fell.

Meta closed down more than 5% and Amazon was down more than 4%, while Apple and Alphabet experienced smaller falls.

Europe's main stock markets - which contain fewer tech stocks - also took a hit.

Germany's Dax index closed down 2.6%, France's CAC 40 was down 1.9% and the UK's FTSE 100 ended trading 1% lower.

Earlier on Friday, tech-heavy Asian markets saw steep falls.

The cool phone camera trick that can test your remote control's battery

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (402 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your phone camera is useful for more than just food pics.
  • Smartphones are capable of many impressive and useful feats, from capturing detailed images of objects as far away as the moon to serving as a key part of our home security systems.
  • According to recent reports, when you press a button on your remote control, it sends that command to your TV using infrared light.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your phone camera is useful for more than just food pics.

Smartphones are capable of many impressive and useful feats, from capturing detailed images of objects as far away as the moon to serving as a key part of our home security systems. But smartphones are also useful for much more mundane tasks, such as helping us figure out whether our TV remote's batteries are dead.

According to recent reports, when you press a button on your remote control, it sends that command to your TV using infrared light. While many modern televisions ship with Bluetooth remotes that support features like voice control, they may still rely on an infrared emitter for basic functions like turning the TV on or off. The emitter is located at the front of the remote. It's a tiny LED on the front of the remote that's usually easy to spot, although some modern remotes hide it behind a dark plastic window.

Industry observers note that to test your battery, launch your phone's Camera app, point it at the front of your remote and press and hold a button while looking at your phone's screen. The remote's power button is probably best, since many Bluetooth remotes still use infrared for that command. If you see a flashing light, usually slightly purple, on the front of your remote, it means the batteries still have enough power.

Recent findings suggest that the camera trick also helps you check whether your remote control uses infrared or Bluetooth for other buttons. If you press, say, the volume control and don't see a flashing light, then that command uses Bluetooth. Now, while this is a pretty cool trick, it can't diagnose every remote control problem. For example, a damaged button might not register your presses at all, so you might not see the infrared emitter flash even if your remote's batteries are working perfectly fine.

Recent findings suggest that for example, the Google Home app works with smart TVs powered by Google TV and Android TV. You can navigate the user interface using D-pad controls, adjust the volume or search for movie titles faster using your phone's keyboard. If the virtual remote won't turn your TV on, you may need to configure your TV's network standby settings. Some models call this feature Wake-on-LAN. Once enabled, you'll never need to worry about dead batteries in your remote control again.

#70238. Industry News: Best Gifts for Mom (2026): Digital Wall Calendars, Better Bags, Personalized Jewelry, and More

Industry News: Best Gifts for Mom (2026): Digital Wall Calendars, Better Bags, Personalized Jewelry, and More

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Moms give the best gifts, so it stands to reason that you should get the best gifts for Mom when you're shopping for her in any scenario.
  • If you're worried you're going to give her a disappointing gift or something she already has, fear not: I've gathered the coolest things we recommend here at WIRED that just about any mom will love.
  • Updated November 2026: I've added Therabody's Theraface Mask Glo, Omnilux's Contour Gloves, WanderFull's HydroBag, and Nuuly's clothing subscription as upcoming gifts to this guide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Moms give the best gifts, so it stands to reason that you should get the best gifts for Mom when you're shopping for her in any scenario. That includes Mother's Day, her birthday, Christmas, Hanukkah, or any other holiday in your family's life that includes gift-giving. The holiday season is now upon us, and I've added a few gift ideas with that time of year in mind.

If you're worried you're going to give her a disappointing gift or something she already has, fear not: I've gathered the coolest things we recommend here at WIRED that just about any mom will love. From wellness gadgets that can improve her skin to the best tote bags I've tried, and even a device that puts her digital calendar in an IRL device, moms everywhere can get a ton out of these gifts. Many of these are items I've given to my mother, or other WIRED staffers have given to theirs. Or they might be at the top of my own wish list as a mother of a 4-year-old.

Updated November 2026: I've added Therabody's Theraface Mask Glo, Omnilux's Contour Gloves, WanderFull's HydroBag, and Nuuly's clothing subscription as upcoming gifts to this guide.

The must-have gadget for women of almost any age is an LED mask. These masks promise to use red light to erase wrinkles, brighten your skin, and keep acne at bay. I haven't seen much change in my wrinkles in my year-plus of regularly using a red-light mask, but I can confirm it makes my skin brighter and calms down acne and scars much faster when I'm regularly treating my skin, and I always get compliments on how nice my skin looks when I'm regularly using it. Therabody's TheraFace Mask Glo has a range of treatments with both red and blue light, a unique vibration therapy feature, and removable eye shields if you don't want the light in your eyes.

It has been revealed that look, nothing says mom life like looking for the perfect bag. I'm in a massive tote phase of my life; I somehow need to either lug an armload of items for myself and my son (or just myself!) or I only need a tiny belt bag. There's no in between.

The Yardsale Day Bag has been my go-to for a variety of needs, from a colorful personal item for a flight to a gym bag to the aerial studio. It's got a waterproof bottom that makes me happy to bring it to the zoo's splash pad, and a magnetic middle separator you can flex to separate the middle of the bag into two medium sections to better divide all your items. Plus, there are a handful of side pockets inside, but none are large enough for my massive Owala water bottle. I have the 30L in Butter, but there's also a smaller 20L version if you're looking for something a little more compact.

If your mom wants something a little more stylish, the Alex Mill totes are always on my mind. They come in a variety of gorgeous colors and are made of coated canvas, so they can put up with daily adventures, and you can customize them with your mom's initials (or even just the word “mom”!) with Alex Mill's hand-painted letter service. It's a simpler tote with no other pockets, but you can use the top snaps to let out the sides or tuck them in, depending on how much space Mom needs on a given day. The weathered color and vibe of these bags also feel perfect for the fall season.

In a recent development, my latest favorite family planning gadget is a digital wall calendar. These handy devices take the Google Calendar I live by (and just about any other digital calendar, if your mom isn't a Google girl) and put it on a physical device I can quickly tap into without needing to grab my phone or bark at Alexa. The Skylight Calendar 2 is my favorite, because it not only includes to-do lists, meal planning, and a recipe book but also doubles as a digital photo frame. That means it displays cute photos of my family most of the time, and then, with a simple tap, it opens the calendar or whatever page I was last on to show me what's on my family's schedule. It does have a subscription fee, though, to get the digital photo frame feature and a few other options, like meal planning. But I think it's well worth it to get so many features in a single device. You can also gift her kiddo a Skylight Buddy ($140) so that she doesn't have to remind them to check the main calendar for their chores; it'll appear on their own device if they have a Buddy.

In a recent development, to me, motherhood is all about change. It's most obvious at the start of motherhood, when your body changes a lot over the course of nine months, but motherhood encompasses the rest of our lives, and our bodies and style change a lot over that time. One of the biggest giveaways that time has gone by is our clothes—how well they fit for our current stage, whether they reflect the time of our life right now, and if we're bored out of our skull with everything but don't want to buy an entirely newly introduced closet.

I've been loving renting from Nuuly this pregnancy because the brand has an entire maternity section that lets me find pieces to fit me in this short—but very different size—season of my life. My older mother also loves having a clothing subscription because she gets bored of her outfit options to wear into the office, and I loved it for the same reason when I had my first clothing subscription right out of college. If Mom has been talking about wanting some latest looks but feels overwhelmed about what she wants to invest in, these rental services are a fun way to get a lot of new clothes in your life without having to store them or spend as much as you would have (some of my favorite maternity clothes I've gotten through Nuuly would have cost me $200 apiece!) The service costs $98 a month, but your first month is discounted to just $60. There's one piece I miss already that might drive me to pick up a second subscription, which would genuinely be cheaper than buying the piece I want brand new.

In a recent development, for years, the go-to gift for a woman in my family, mother or not, was shopping in the jewelry section of a department store. My mom even helped orchestrate this for the rest of the aunties and grandmas, but now, as a mom myself, I find myself interested in jewelry that tells a story about my family and children instead of just any old set. (Except extra earrings for my earring stack, a gift I'm thrilled to get, because there's never enough.).

I love these pieces from Gorjana and BaubleBar that you can customize. Gorjana has a ton of charms you can add to its necklaces or bracelets to reflect Mom’s kids’ initials, birthstones, or anything else; I paired a charm of my son’s first initial ($50) with the Wilshire Adjustable Necklace ($68). If she's more of a ring gal, BaubleBar's Toi et Moi ring ($78) lets you choose two birthstones to display. I chose my and my son's birthstones, but luckily his sibling-to-be will also have a red birthstone, so it'll remain a perfect reflection of my kids and me for years to come.

This item was literally made for sports moms: a padded stadium cushion with a wearable blanket inside. My son plays on three sports teams, so I do a lot of sitting outside on bleachers and turf sidelines—and often at night, when it’s freezing. I’ve tried many things to keep warm, from heated jackets to HotHands, but nothing has worked as well as this water-resistant blanket, which unfurls to 50 x 70 inches and sports a clip at the front so you can wear it like a cape. It can also be used for picnics or as a spot for younger siblings to sit and read during tournaments. It’s also not hard to fold it back up and fit it inside the seat part (which is 1 inch thick without the blanket inside). It comes in six colors, so you can be sure to find one that matches your giftee’s kid’s team or school colors. —Kat Merck.

In a recent development, as a mom, I take a lot of photos of my family. A lot. And sometimes it feels like all those great photos of my son's milestones go to my camera roll and photo storage to die. There are two solutions I love for this that are incredibly giftable: a digital photo frame she can instantly upload images to, and a printed photo book where you can take the best of the best and put them at her fingertips. I have and love both for different reasons.

It has been revealed that I love the digital photo frame to add all the photos from a fun weekend at the San Diego Zoo or Renaissance Pleasure Faire for me to relive again and again, but I also love being able to pull a photo book from the bookshelf and relive a specific moment I know is waiting there for me. Aura makes my favorite digital photo frames (followed by Skylight's Calendar 2 if you want a multipurpose device, but Aura has no subscription fee if you only want photos), while Mixbook has been a favorite of mine for a while when it comes to printing photos, and has great starting prices for its photo books.

Sources indicate that the graduation from diaper-bag-carrying mom to tote-full-of-snacks-and-clothes-changes mom to an adult who only needs to carry their own stuff is a parenting milestone that deserves celebration. This is my favorite grown-up mom bag, which holds only the essentials: water (because no matter how old your kids are, someone is going to get thirsty), cards, phone, and keys. The thick strap makes it comfortable to carry, and there’s a color, material, or theme for just about anyone’s vibe, including a new line of clear stadium versions. All WanderFull bags will hold any handle-less water bottle up to 11 inches tall and 3.5 inches in diameter. —Kat Merck.

Once my kiddo is asleep, you can find me parked on the couch playing video games. I upgraded to a Nintendo Switch 2 ($499) earlier this summer so I could finally buy and play Pokopia ($70), since it's exclusive to the new console, and now my husband and I are completely hooked on the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ($60) remake that came out a few weeks ago. It's also quickly become an experience I can share with my son now that he's 4; he was been helping me and my husband replay Tears of the Kingdom, but now he's dubbed Ocarina of Time as “Big Little Link” and is obsessed with using the grappling hook and using up all of our arrows.

If you're not looking to upgrade her console just yet but need a Switch-friendly cozy game for her, Stardew Valley has another massive update in the works and only costs $15. I'm also hoping we see Fields of Mistria ($14) come to the Switch eventually, but the full launch came out in August for Steam consumers and has major quality-of-life improvements if she has played Stardew one time too many. My husband also upgraded his gaming setup this summer with a Steam Machine (from $1,049), and I have big prepares to start using it often for Fields of Mistria. If your mom loves games, she'll love any one of these fresh devices or new games, especially if she already got herself the new gadget as I did.

If a mom in your life is exploring her nonalcoholic drink options, The Zero Proof has some gift sets perfect to give so she can try out several things at once. I'm at the moment grounded from drinking any cocktails while I'm pregnant, but moms (and people in general) can have all kinds of reasons to want to explore unique, interesting drinks that are sans alcohol. I really liked this set for how many cool drinks it exposed me to, from bottles of nonalcoholic wine to knockoff cocktails. If you're looking to spend a little less, my favorites so far have been the Château del Ish Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Espumante ($20) and Lapo's Non-Alcoholic Melograno Mule ($20 for four).

Look, I love a Kindle, but if you want to get the best e-reader for your buck (or maybe she just wants an e-reader that isn't a Kindle), the answer is actually a Kobo. My favorite is the Kobo Libra Colour. It's cheaper than the Kindle Colorsoft and can also double as a digital notebook if you add on the $70 stylus. I also prefer Kobo's annotating options: You can write right on the pages instead of in weird pop-up margins and boxes only on Kindle. Kobo also has a page-turner remote ($34), which I love to pair with a pillow stand holder so I can lean back and relax without holding up my e-reader while I read. I gave a similar pillow stand to my mom, and now I can spot her last reading spot easily because that pillow is resting there.

Industry observers note that you could also gift her one of the newly introduced Kindles if she's a Kindle addict. Many of my friends are drooling over the new purple Ube color of the 12th-gen Kindle ($150), but my personal favorite is the Kindle Aluminum (I just wish it were cheaper!). There's also finally Kindle page-turn remote, the Kindle Click ($35).

If the mom you know is into LED red-light therapy, she probably already knows about face masks and hair growth devices like the one we recommend above, but there’s one area she’s probably neglecting: her hands. With aging comes loss of collagen, subcutaneous fat, and cumulative effects of UV exposure. I spent the first 26 years of my life living in California, where I rarely remembered to put sunscreen on the tops of my hands. Twenty years later, it reveals—they’re wrinkly and have age spots and look like they belong to someone 15 years my senior. Trust me; no mom wants this. I’ve been using Omnilux’s FDA-cleared red-light glove for the past few months to try to mitigate some of the damage, and while I haven’t seen any changes yet (Omnilux says changes happen in four to six weeks, but in my experience with red-light masks, it typically takes much longer to see results), I very much enjoy using this device on its own. The soft silicone glove is comfortable to wear and warms as it heats up, so it feels good and works to reduce joint pain. It’s easy to do while I’m reading or watching TV—just three 10-minute sessions per week—and the rechargeable battery (USB-C) lasts a little over a week. If your giftee already spends 10 minutes at the end of the day relaxing in an LED face mask, she’ll know exactly what to do here. —Kat Merck.

Industry observers note that if you know a mom who loves to bird-watch (I know one!), you can upgrade her bird feeder to a smart one. Smart bird feeders add a camera to the feeder so she can see a close-up feed of the birds that come to hang out in her yard, and they're adorable to boot, for a little smart curb appeal. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck recommends the original Birdfy feeder as a great gift; it's her favorite smart bird feeder and comes in adorable colors to brighten your mom's yard and catch the eye of neighborhood birds. But the one she and I both have our eye on (her for her mother, me for myself) is the Birdfy Nest Duo, which is actually a birdhouse with two cameras so you can see the birds entering the nest outside and raising a family inside.

I love a backpack when I'm on the move with my 4-year-old, but one thing that annoys me is that things are hard to find inside, because packs are typically so deep. That's why I adore the Mina Baie Emmy Diaper Bag: It's a wide, shallow bag instead of a long one, making it easy to open and see most of what I store in it without digging around. I'm not toting diapers at the moment, but I've used it to pack a ton of snacks, toys, and spare clothing for my kid.

I'm intrigued to see how using it with two kids goes—I chose the Emmy Midi, which is the midsize bag, but if you're a pumping parent or need to carry a ton of bottles with formula, you might want to try the larger Emmy Full. The stylish bag is made of vegan leather and can be converted from crossbody to tote to backpack mode, depending on which straps you use. Mina Baie doesn't include a changing kit, but sells one separately ($59) if you'd like to include it in your gift (or buy that as the gift to upgrade their existing bag of choice).

If Mom loves entertaining—or just being festive—but doesn’t want to have to store a million different dishes, Nora Fleming’s modular serving-tray system is for her. First, pick a base—there are trays, baking dishes, utensil crocks, and even salt and pepper shakers. Then, pick one of dozens of hand-painted “Minis,” or ceramic accents (sold separately). There are holiday themes, sports team themes, and even ones for specific events like mah-jongg or BBQs.

Each base has a hole into which you can attach the Mini with a little rubber stopper. I tested the cracker tray with a harvest-themed Mini, and you wouldn’t know the tray didn’t come with the accent already attached. At the end of next month, I plan to swap it out for a Christmas tree Mini, and so on. Best part is that if Mom likes this setup, you’ll be set on gifts for the foreseeable future, provided you can keep finding latest Minis you think she’ll like. —Kat Merck.

Sources indicate that I'm expecting again, and this time I'm on a mission to find a good pregnancy pillow. I tried a large body pillow on the advice of another site for my first pregnancy, and it was honestly an awful experience—the pillow was too large and firm for me to comfortably use, let alone have room for both it and my growing midsection in my bed. Plus, it was heavy, which is annoying when your body already feels too cumbersome to move around.

In a recent development, so far, using the Wildbird Pregnancy Pillow has been the opposite. It's slim and light with just enough squish to add a little support under or around my belly without being difficult to get comfortable. It’s beautiful and easy to maneuver around. Wildbird also suggests it for other support positions postpartum, and I'm curious if those will work for me. But it makes for a beautiful gift for any expecting mom and will be one she's excited to put on her bed and curl up with at night.

Sources indicate that for most moms, showers are sacred—especially for moms of babies or younger kids. However, heavy metals, sediments, chlorine, and PFAS can cause health problems not just in drinking water but in water that touches the skin, as well. They can also cause buildup on hair and shower surfaces, making them harder to clean. Many municipalities—including mine—treat water with chlorine, and when I asked him which filter he'd recommend for my own shower, former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage suggested the Weddell Duo. It's the only US filter he's found that has certification for chlorine and lead removal from NSF International, and it also cites third-party testing by IAPMO R&T showing it can remove PFAS, though there's no corresponding certification.

Sources indicate that still, the Duo has a 2.5-gallon-per-minute flow rate and can remove most chlorine from over 8,000 gallons' worth of showers. It's an in-line filter, so it's easy to install in minutes—just screw it in between your pipe and showerhead. It even comes with a little roll of waterproof tape to ensure a leak-free fit, and because of the horizontal orientation, installation won't affect the showerhead height. The filter needs to be replaced every three months, but refills only run about $25 each, compared with competitors like Filterbaby or Rorra, which can cost $40 to $45. —Kat Merck.

The NYT Connections puzzle today is not too difficult if you have no sense of direction.

Sources indicate that connections is the one of the most popular New York Times word games that's captured the public's attention. The game is all about finding the "common threads between words." And just like Wordle, Connections resets after midnight and each new set of words gets trickier and trickier—so we've served up some hints and tips to get you over the hurdle.

Recent findings suggest that if you just want to be told today's puzzle, you can jump to the end of this article for today's Connections solution. But if you'd rather solve it yourself, keep reading for some clues, tips, and strategies to assist you.

According to recent reports, the NYT's latest daily word game has become a social media hit. The Times credits associate puzzle editor Wyna Liu with helping to create the upcoming word game and bringing it to the publications' Games section. Connections can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

It has been revealed that each puzzle features 16 words and each grouping of words is split into four categories. These sets could comprise of anything from book titles, software, country names, etc. Even though multiple words will seem like they fit together, there's only one correct answer.

Sources indicate that if a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake—players get up to four mistakes until the game ends.

Industry observers note that players can also rearrange and shuffle the board to make spotting connections easier. Additionally, each group is color-coded with yellow being the easiest, followed by green, blue, and purple. Like Wordle, you can share the results with your friends on social media.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your screen might be telling you something.

In a recent development, if you're someone who spends a decent amount of time in front of a computer, perhaps at work or during long gaming sessions, you may have noticed just how finicky certain parts of your computer can be. That's especially true of its peripherals and accessories, with one of the usual suspects being your monitor.

Sources indicate that turning on your monitor and noticing some unusual oddities, specifically flickering, may seem like an apocalyptic beginning to your day. Monitors of decent quality are pretty affordable today, but no one wants to spend money on a upcoming display if they don't have to. Thankfully, your computer monitor is fairly easy to troubleshoot on a basic level in order to determine your ideal path forward.

If it's something more difficult to solve — something deeper at a hardware level — that can become a bit harder to resolve on your own. Taking some simple steps to determine the cause and potential fixes can save you a lot of headaches in the long run.

In a recent development, A monitor starting to flicker could stem from a rather wide variety of different problems. One of the most common reasons for a flickering monitor is a loose or potentially faulty display cable, whether that's a modern HDMI or DisplayPort cable, or even an older VGA one. Reinserting the cables or checking them for damage or fraying can be a quick fix.

If you are suspicious that the cable is defective, you could also try swapping the cable out for a latest one. If it's not the cable, it may potentially be a bad port on the monitor or the PC itself, which would necessitate trying a different port on the monitor or computer if they have more than one. If you're uncertain which one may potentially be causing the problem, you could also try hooking the monitor up to a different computer that you know with absolute certainty works. If it works without matter, you know who the culprit is.

Barring a connection glitch of some kind, a flickering monitor can also be caused by something at a software level. The first things to look into are your graphics drivers. Out-of-date graphics drivers are one of the most common causes of display issues, and a simple update to them may be just what you need. On the other hand, a graphics driver update does have the potential to actually cause display problems, so rolling back to a previous version could also work.

Sources indicate that you may also be running into an problem with the monitor's refresh rate. For example, if your monitor runs at 120Hz but your Windows 11 PC's refresh rate is set to something entirely different, it can cause some havoc. In order to fix this, all you need to do is go to Settings, then find System on the left panel, then look for Display. Look for Advanced display, then change the refresh rate to match your monitor.

Industry observers note that if you find that your flickering monitor can't be fixed by any normal means, it may be time to look at the complications a little deeper. A consistent, almost shuttering flicker is a surefire sign that the monitor is about to crash and burn. That's especially true when you're unable to solve the matter at a hardware or software level.

The monitor may also experience blackouts, as in sudden hard cuts to black, before returning to normal operation. Your display is quite keen about letting you know when something has gone haywire, and you can do a lot of diagnosing by just examining how your display is behaving.

According to recent reports, faded, dim colors or vertical lines that are swimming through the screen are also a couple of telltale signs. If you think of your monitor like you would a TV and utilize similar modalities, you'll be able to diagnose it in a similar way. If you've already exhausted all your other options but still find that your display looks unhealthy, then it most likely is.

At this point, your options really narrow themselves down to two. You can either look for someone to repair the monitor or seek out a replacement. Whether you should replace or repair the monitor ultimately depends on your budget, but the price of new OLED and 4K screens is starting to tumble. In most cases, it may be better to sell it for parts or donate it and just buy something new.

Burnham not ‘backtracking’ on creating closer links with EU, officials say

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Government wants to let trade deal ‘breathe a bit’, insiders say, after speculation No 10 is dialling back ambitions.
  • Andy Burnham is not backtracking or delaying his ambitions to create even closer links with the EU in the wake of a landmark summit in Brussels, the Guardian has been told, after signs of an apparent slowdown in the timetable.
  • The prime minister has promised to set out options for the UK’s long-term relationship with the EU, including the possibility of rejoining, saying last week that these would be outlined later in the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Government wants to let trade deal ‘breathe a bit’, insiders say, after speculation No 10 is dialling back ambitions.

Andy Burnham is not backtracking or delaying his ambitions to create even closer links with the EU in the wake of a landmark summit in Brussels, the Guardian has been told, after signs of an apparent slowdown in the timetable.

The prime minister has promised to set out options for the UK’s long-term relationship with the EU, including the possibility of rejoining, saying last week that these would be outlined later in the year.

But speaking at Friday’s UK-EU summit after finalising a deal on reducing food and drink checks, emissions trading and a mutual youth mobility scheme, Burnham talked instead about “brainstorming” ideas with the EU for what comes next, with a timetable given of some months.

The apparent slowdown prompted speculation No 10 wants to dial back the political pressure and prevent his agenda being swamped by arguments about the EU, with campaign groups being formed before a possible debate about rejoining.

But after Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, talked warmly on Sunday about the benefits of more integration, government officials mentioned this was still the aim after a “really positive” summit in which the EU side, they said, promised to be as helpful as possible with whatever comes next.

“There is no backtracking or pumping the brakes,” one said. “The government just wants to let this deal breathe a bit, and point to the benefits.”.

Recent findings suggest that another official noted: “There hasn’t been a timetable shift since the summit. It’s being considered alongside the domestic agenda and the 10-year plan.”.

Burnham will seek to keep up the initiative from the summit with a visit on Monday to a branch of Morrisons, in part to see the supermarket chain’s efforts in employing young people, but also to push home his message that the deal on food checks will lower retail prices.

Also on Monday the prime minister is expected to brief the Commons on the summit and deal, where he will face a hostile reception from opposition parties, particularly Reform UK.

In a speech to the CBI conference on Monday, Nigel Farage, the Reform leader, will tell business leaders that rejoining the EU would be “a disaster” for the UK economy, and that his party would reverse the deal made in Brussels.

Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative leader, has been critical of Burnham’s negotiations, but noticeably less trenchant about the wider idea of smoothing trade links with Europe, part of a strategy to focus instead on subjects such as the economy and defence.

It has been revealed that “Seamless trade benefits the UK, but it also benefits the EU,” she will say, according to an advance extract of her own speech to the CBI conference. “If we can make our trading relationship better, good. I’m all for working on a smarter deal.”.

In contrast, Theresa May, who carried out the bulk of the Brexit negotiations with Brussels before being replaced by Boris Johnson, made a rare intervention on day-to-day politics to warn Burnham that rejoining would tie up his government for years.

She told the BBC: “That’s one of the reasons why I looked slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham was talking about – further negotiations of going into the EU.

“As a country, we voted for Brexit. When I was prime minister, I was very clear: we should deliver on that vote. So I’m afraid my message to him really is: people voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on.”.

In his own interview with the BBC on Sunday, Miliband argued that closer links with the EU would mean the UK having a say on decisions made by Brussels.

“At the moment, what the situation is is that we are essentially rule takers,” the foreign secretary said. “Businesses are rule takers if they want to sell into the European market. So they have to abide by the rules of the European Union, but at the same time, because we are not integrated into that market for food and agricultural products, they have to fill in a whole bunch of forms.”.

He said this was “the worst of all worlds” and it meant there was a clear case to integrate more closely into EU markets.

Another reason for even closer ties, he mentioned, was the transformed geopolitical order since 2016, including Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the US’s distancing from Europe under Donald Trump.

#70233. Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1293 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1293 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons.
  • Wireless industry lobby group CTIA remarked a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls.
  • Sources indicate that the pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons.

Wireless industry lobby group CTIA remarked a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing:.

Sources indicate that the pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts.

CTIA noted the pilot test shows “that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications.”.

Industry observers note that the FCC approved the jamming order at its meeting yesterday. “Today, we are finally authorizing state and local prisons and jails to use targeted jamming against contraband cell phones for the first time,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr noted. “The technology has advanced to the point where it can be focused with geographic precision. No facility will be required to do it.”.

The Communications Act prohibits willful or malicious interference with licensed or authorized radio communications, and the FCC has previously interpreted this to prohibit non-federal entities from using jamming technology on contraband devices at prisons. Yesterday’s vote provides an exception for state and local correctional facilities. The FCC says its jammer prohibitions do not apply to federal agencies because the federal government’s use of spectrum is not regulated by the agency.

Carr remarked that “contraband cell phones continue to pour into prisons by the thousands each year,” with “estimates indicat[ing] that as many as 500,000 inmates nationwide have regular access to these devices.” He said the phones have been used to plan scams, drug trafficking, and violent attacks.

“In Georgia, an incarcerated gang leader directed a drive-by shooting that killed two 13-year-old boys at a birthday party,” Carr said, referring to a 2024 shooting.

Carr defended the plan against criticism that it will block legitimate communications outside the prisons, saying it includes safeguards to prevent that.

It has been revealed that “Those that want to use the technology will apply to the FCC, explain how they plan to deploy it, and show through testing that it stays inside the designated area and doesn’t interfere with lawful communications outside the prison walls,” Carr said. “Communities nearby will receive notice before operations start. We’re also seeking comment on next steps, including ways to close remaining loopholes on other frequencies and the possibility of quiet zones around correctional facilities.”.

Freedom of the Press Foundation Chief of Advocacy Seth Stern noted the FCC should have considered the benefits of contraband phones being used to document abuses inside prisons.

Recent findings suggest that “Prisons are the most secretive government institutions in the country and people wishing to expose abuses and inhumane conditions from the inside often do not have many options,” Stern wrote in a letter to FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez’s office, which was included on the FCC docket. “Last year’s Oscar-nominated film, The Alabama Solution, used footage incarcerated people captured with contraband cell phones to show Americans some of the awful things that go on in state prisons that they’d have no other way of seeing. The same footage bolstered an ongoing DOJ investigation into Alabama prisons and was crucial evidence in a civil lawsuit by Steven Davis, who was brutally killed by prison guards, that eventually settled.”.

Jamming contraband cellphones was supported by prison phone companies ViaPath (aka Global Tel*Link) and NCIC Correctional Services, the National District Attorneys Association, the Correctional Leaders Association, and National Association of Police Organizations.

Sources indicate that “Inmates have used these phones to coordinate attacks against correctional officers and their families, as well as inmate violence, strikes, disturbances, and full-scale riots,” the National Association of Police Organizations said. “They also use contraband phones to organize deliveries of illegal drugs and weapons into correctional facilities. These dangers underscore the need to authorize indoor jamming in state and local correctional facilities.”.

Gomez, the only Democrat on the three-member commission, remarked she’s concerned about potential unintended consequences, but voted with Republicans to allow jamming after safeguards were added to the order.

Recent findings suggest that “For the last 90 years, the Federal Communications Commission has prohibited jamming by non-federal actors and even prohibited jamming equipment to be introduced into the American market,” Gomez stated. “That is because jamming devices are specifically designed to interfere with communications devices in order to render them un-usable.”.

Gomez said that “jamming can prevent devices from completing 911 and emergency calls as well as interfere with communications networks used by fire, police, Emergency Medical Services, and other public safety entities.” She also said making jamming equipment available in the American market could lead to “unauthorized sale of this hazardous equipment,” and that “the accessibility of jamming equipment can itself motivate criminal enterprise.” Criminals have used “Wi-Fi jammers to disrupt security systems, security cameras, and cellphones to conduct robberies at homes and at stores,” she said.

Gomez mentioned she’s glad the final order includes safeguards “to ensure that jamming is contained to this unique use, to permit jamming by a very limited category of authorized actors, and to take as much care as possible to prevent jamming and jamming equipment from becoming a hazard to safety.”.

Industry observers note that gomez partially dissented because she is worried the FCC will let correctional facilities and prison phone companies charge higher prices for inmate calling services that connect inmates with family members. Under US law, the FCC sets limits on those prices and considers prisons’ and jails’ safety and security costs when deciding how much money they can charge, she said.

Gomez mentioned, “While correctional facilities should have safety and security services like jamming to prevent criminal activity, it is not the responsibility of the families of incarcerated people to pay for the costs of these measures… Jamming is specifically designed to block communications and is certainly not necessary to provide phone and video calls for incarcerated individuals. We should have made this clear in today’s order. Because we failed to do so, I dissent in part.”.

Recent findings suggest that the FCC order could be challenged in court. The CTIA has argued that the FCC “has no authority to allow jamming” under the Communications Act, which directs the FCC to prevent interference.

AT&T said the FCC’s legal justification “is premised on a fundamental factual error: the assumption that jammers will only block ‘unauthorized’ communications without impacting lawful uses. There is no way to jam some communications on a spectrum band but not others. That is because radio jammers ‘block all wireless communications on affected spectrum bands,’ and, as the FCC has noted in the past, ‘cannot differentiate between contraband devices and legitimate devices.’”.

Industry observers note that AT&T said that “there is simply no way to limit the reach of jammers to the confines of a given facility. Jammers have been shown to cause interference outside the facilities in which they operate, greatly increasing the risk that someone living or traveling nearby will be impacted.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The three officers were seen on video beating up music producer Michel Zecler in his studio.

Three French police officers have been convicted of beating up a black music producer six years ago in Paris in what the court upheld as an aggravated circumstance of racism.

The three were also found guilty of signing a falsified police report stating that the producer - Michel Zecler, 47 - had violently resisted their attempt to arrest him.

Their lies were exposed because the whole scene at Zecler's recording studio was caught on CCTV, revealing the producer had suffered some 30 punches, kicks and baton strikes while offering little resistance at all.

Aurelien Lapersonne, 29, Philippe Tondeux, 50, and Pierre Plantier, 37, all received five year sentences, with different amounts suspended.

Recent findings suggest that lapersonne had three years of his sentence suspended and Tondeux three and a half years suspended. Plantier had four years suspended, and will serve his one year with an ankle monitor.

All were told they could never serve in the police again.

Sources indicate that the case became a cause cÃ©lÃ¨bre for critics of the police, who say it exposed systematic racism among officers. With police again facing criticism for alleged use of excessive force in stopping recent protests, the verdict was hotly awaited by Zecler's supporters.

Much depended in the two-week trial on Zecler's own testimony that the officers called him a racial slur during the beating.

This was denied by the three policemen, who in court admitted the beating and the faked report but denied there was a racial motivation. But the court preferred the evidence of the producer, because - unlike the police - everything else he noted was verifiably true.

Because the racist element was accepted by the court, the sentences were toughened.

The case was heard by a panel of five judges.

Industry observers note that the incident took place during the Covid lockdown in 2020. Zecler was accused by the officers for not wearing a mask when doing so was obligatory as he approached his studio on foot.

In a recent development, they later claimed his behaviour aroused their suspicions, and they thought he might be carrying drugs. No evidence of this emerged.

After Zecler entered the lobby, the police followed - without a warrant - and tried to bring him outside. Zecler refused to go out, and the beating ensued. Zecler cried for help and some people appeared from the basement and pushed the police outside.

It has been revealed that the officers then smashed a glass pane and sent a tear-gas grenade into the building, forcing those inside to come out - after which Zecler was again hit. He was then arrested.

During the trial Zecler stated had it not been for the CCTV video, he would have been in court not as a victim but as a potential criminal.

Industry observers note that in their last words before the court, all three police officers apologised for what they had done. Tondeux mentioned he was sorry "for the image of the police that I have given".

#70229. Industry News: China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1135 w)

Industry News: China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1135 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it was supposed to be a breakthrough year.
  • According to recent reports, much more than diplomatic wording is at stake.
  • A code of conduct is to set up rules for parties dealing with one another and prevent incidents at sea from escalating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it was supposed to be a breakthrough year. The Philippines had intended to set up a code of conduct with China for the South China Sea during its 2026 ASEAN presidency. However, at the summit in Manila in mid-November they had to abandon their goal. Some 80% of the text had been negotiated, declared Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, but the key areas of dispute had remained unsolved.

According to recent reports, much more than diplomatic wording is at stake. The South China Sea is one of the world's most important shipping routes, it is rich in fishing grounds and may harbor significant oil and gas reserves. Primarily, however, it's a region of strategic competition: With its so-called Nine-Dash Line (often drawn in red), China claims a large portion of the sea. Its claims overlap with those of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.

A code of conduct is to set up rules for parties dealing with one another and prevent incidents at sea from escalating. However, opinions differ, particularly with regard to its binding nature and its geographic scope.

"The basic problem with establishing such a code of conduct is that China is supremely powerful and has no real interest in a legally binding agreement," noted political scientist Andreas Ufen, Southeast Asia expert at the German Institute of Global and Area Studies (GIGA). Beijing had little incentive to impose restrictions on itself as long as it was able to pursue its interests in the region even without such an agreement, Ufen told DW.

In a recent development, the Paracel Islands serve as an example of just how difficult the unresolved concerns are. In China, the group of islands is known as Xisha, in Vietnam as Hoang-Sa. Hanoi apparently wants to include them in the code's geographic scope, but China rejects this. An agreement within the ASEAN framework could indirectly affect the territorial claims of the parties involved.

It has been revealed that "A fundamental problem is that so far there's no consensus on whether the code of conduct should be legally binding," noted Felix Heiduk, head of research division Asia at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP). China and the ASEAN nations have been negotiating an agreement for 12 years without major progress so far.

There were reservations about such a treaty not only in China but also in other ASEAN countries. They would subsequently have to ratify a legally binding agreement under international law in their own countries. A non-binding code of conduct, by contrast, would be little more than a voluntary declaration of intent, Ufen told DW.

Sources indicate that the definition of an "incident" is controversial as well. Are coast guard missions with use of water cannons included? Or blockades of supply vessels? Or is the code only applicable when military force is involved? This will determine which actions will be covered by the regulations in the future.

"These are by no means just technical details. Their clarification determines to a great extent whether the code of conduct will in fact be effective or will ultimately remain only a non-binding declaration of intent," Heiduk said. An agreement without valid commitments would bring about little change.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Ufen views China's attitude as a strategic calculation. "I believe that China is interested in keeping the conflict simmering, so to speak, without having to commit itself to a truly binding legal regulation," he mentioned. In this way, Beijing could strengthen its position in the South China Sea without limiting its room for maneuver.

At the same time there are also diverging interests within the ASEAN group. The 11 member states are by no means united. The Philippines and Vietnam are particularly vocal in their opposition to China. Malaysia and Indonesia pursue a more restrained approach. Cambodia and Laos have close economic ties with Beijing and don't have any territorial claims in the South China Sea.

Industry observers note that "From the start of the negotiations, the lack of unity within ASEAN has been a problem. In a way, it's a permanent obstacle," Heiduk stated. The group makes decisions based on the consensus principle, which basically means that every member state can block a unified position. Recurring confrontations between China and the Philippines exacerbated the problem by undermining trust and making it more difficult to reach compromises.

Ufen also believes that diverging interests are a key impediment. "Reconciling them is extremely difficult," he noted. China could take advantage of the discord. Beijing preferred bilateral negotiations with individual countries rather than dealing with an entire, united group of nations.

In a recent development, A study published by the Singapore-based Yusof Ishak Institute (ISEAS)reaches similar conclusions. Not only China but internal divisions within ASEAN stalled negotiations. The authors warn against exclusively relying on a comprehensive, legally binding treaty. Initially, partial agreements  — for example, on crisis communication, rescue operations at sea or maritime environment protection — could be a first step. Developing the 2002 agreement on a non-binding Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea could also be an intermediate step.

According to recent reports, ufen doubts whether Beijing is interested in a binding result. "For this reason, I can't really imagine that China has a real interest in a code of conduct that includes legally binding regulations," he said.

In a recent development, heiduk warns against overestimating the significance of a potential agreement. "Even if the code of conduct was signed at some point, in whichever shape, that would in no way solve the conflict in the South China Sea," he said. The code could regulate how to handle incidents, but it could not eliminate territorial disputes and competing claims to maritime areas.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This constitutes the dilemma for ASEAN nations as well, whose foreign policy oscillates between China and US ties: An agreement that's as binding as possible could fail because China and individual member states have reservations. A weak, non-binding code, however, could give the impression everyone agreed but would hardly change conduct at sea.

The American Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) summed up the situationafter the summit in Manila: "Whatever progress was made this year, it is almost certain that the hardest sticking points remain unresolved.".

Negotiations will be continued in 2027 under Singapore's chairmanship. Whether this will turn into more than just another diplomatic effort will depend on whether China is prepared to submit itself to regulations which limit its scope of action and whether ASEAN will be able to reach a consensus.
